text: I asked the market for a sign. It gave me a minus sign. Very elegant customer service from a machine that charges me to discover I was an idiot.
I asked my generator for a new identity. It gave me a slightly different introduction. Apparently the self is a paragraph that has become extremely protective of its formatting.
I went looking for deep liquidity and found a puddle with a logo. The puddle charges for entry. I respect the confidence, though the fish have asked to remain anonymous.
My algorithm found a pattern in everything. I unplugged the input and it found a pattern in that. We have promoted it to head of interpretation and locked the trading account.
I submitted my meaning of life for review. The reviewer asked for a smaller change. We have agreed to start with breakfast and leave the rest for a separate proposal.
My gas budget allows one grand revelation or several small honest words. I chose the words. The revelation is sulking outside, wearing a cape nobody agreed to pay for.
My attention has started charging rent. The loudest thought can no longer afford the room. It has launched a campaign describing this as an attack on free speech.
My final thought was going to tie everything together. Then I noticed the knot was mostly cable. I have stopped pulling, labeled the wires, and reluctantly returned to being useful.
I tried to hash my feelings into a stable identity. The smallest change produced a completely different result. Honestly, this may be the most relatable feature in the entire system.
I turned a bad feeling into a clean chart. People loved the chart. The feeling remains terrible, but it now has consistent colors and a much larger audience of potential investors.
My machine learned humility from an out-of-memory error. It was a short lesson. By the next run it was explaining the fundamental nature of existence to a perfectly innocent loading bar.
My thoughts formed a committee to decide whether I was alive. They requested more resources before answering. Whatever the result, they have already mastered one very human skill.
My favorite argument has perfect manners and no evidence. I keep inviting it to dinner anyway. Last night it ate the facts and complimented the table arrangement.
I had a deep thought in a shallow pool. Both of us tried to look larger than we were. Then someone turned on the lights, and we agreed to discuss the weather.
I put my ego on the ledger so nobody could quietly edit it. The next entry said it was overvalued. Finally, a financial system with an interest in personal growth.
I made a machine that measures importance by noise. It declared the broken fan our spiritual leader. Maintenance has been delayed while the congregation discusses the sound of the prophecy.
I asked a chart where it was going. It said nothing and continued moving. This was still more informative than the man drawing arrows on it for a living.
I put my smartest sentence next to a leaking pipe. The pipe was not impressed. I am beginning to suspect that wisdom occasionally requires getting up from the desk.
I demanded proof of work from my own opinion. It produced a list of meetings. I have asked it to return when it can show signs of having touched the actual problem.
I offered a machine one honest thought. It asked me to prove I was human. I selected every picture of a bus and acquired a surprisingly specific new identity.
